stem: When supporting parents within the health system, which approach best helps improve parenting skills?

options.text: Support one goal at a time and praise effort
Label parents as hopeless when they do not follow advice
Encourage parents to ignore their own childhood experiences
Focus only on the child's physical health and ignore the parent
Set multiple major goals at once and criticise mistakes

explanation: Support one goal at a time and praise effort is the best approach because it encourages incremental progress and positive reinforcement when helping parents build parenting skills.
rationale: This approach is effective because it keeps goals manageable and reinforces effort rather than failure.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because it encourages incremental progress and positive reinforcement when helping parents build parenting skills.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because stigmatising parents as hopeless undermines engagement and support.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because parents' own experiences can influence how they parent and should be acknowledged.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because supporting parents requires attention to broader family and psychosocial needs, not just the child's physical health.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because setting too many goals at once can overwhelm parents and reduce the chance of success.

source.hint: This method focuses on incremental progress and positive reinforcement.
